I cannot tell whether the system correctly stayed idle or whether the scheduler or journal writer failed silently. An unlogged trading week would be a serious blind spot for a single-bankroll firm.
findings.proposed_change: Cross-check broker or account records for the week against the journal. Proposal: log a heartbeat record for every scheduled run, including runs that produce no decision, so that 'no runs' can be told apart from 'ran, chose cash'.

findings.finding: Because zero runs were recorded, none of this week's audit checks can be performed. That covers strategy drift, risk-limit pressure, approve-all or veto-all patterns, edge-of-bounds operator proposals, and in-sample-only variants. An empty log is not evidence that any of these are absent.
findings.proposed_change: Treat this week as unaudited rather than clean. Proposal: alert the operator when a week ends with zero runs, so that downtime gets fixed instead of being read as a valid cash decision.

findings.finding: There are no decisions, exits or outcomes, so the LLM filter's stated confidence cannot be compared with realised results this week.
findings.proposed_change: Carry calibration review forward to the next week that has resolved exits. Proposal: keep a rolling multi-week calibration window so that sparse weeks do not reset the assessment.

findings.finding: ai_cost_usd is 0 and llm_calls is 0, so there was no AI cost creep this week. Zero cost alongside zero decisions gives no information about cost efficiency.
findings.proposed_change: No change needed. Keep monitoring cost per decision once activity resumes.

findings.finding: shadow_vs_primary is null, so there is no shadow comparison to judge whether the LLM filter adds value over the rules-only baseline.
findings.proposed_change: Proposal: make sure the shadow (rules-only) track runs and is journaled alongside the primary whenever runs execute, so the LLM's added value can be measured net of its cost.

review.assessment: I cannot assess it. The journal records 0 decisions, 0 LLM calls, $0 AI cost and no shadow_vs_primary comparison, so there is no evidence either way about whether the LLM filter improves net results over the rules-only system. Next, confirm whether the system actually ran this week, then judge LLM value from a populated shadow comparison net of call costs.
